title: NEXT: execute the evaluation-engines plan for bbf921j-4qm (start at Task 0; use subagent-driven execution)
description:
RESUME HERE. Design and implementation plan are written and the design is approved by the owner (2026-10-18). Nothing in the plan has been built yet.

READ FIRST (in this order)
1. docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-evaluation-engines-design.md  (approved design: selectable engines, shared result graph, decisions)
2. docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-18-evaluation-engines.md  (19 tasks, phases 0-4; the plan to execute)
3. Beads bbf921j-4qm (the parent issue: the rule reasoner should drive evaluation over the ontology).

WHAT THE OWNER DECIDED
- Startup option intent.evaluator=java|jena|compare, default java; the Jena engine reports NOT READY until the whole conformance corpus passes on it.
- Both engines write the SAME result graph defined by the TM Forum PDFs: explicit rdf:value true/false on intents, expectations and conditions; chosen target members; icm:reason; linked observation triples. icm:result is NOT in the graph: the handler builds TR290 reports (icm:result lives only in reports).
- Keep the Java evaluator alongside the rules and compare them (conformance suite + compare mode).
- chooseFrom is implemented as a Jena rule; allocation write-back stays Java.
- Keep the container-argument extension of set:resourcesWithPropertyObject in both engines as a documented project extension.
- The licensed ontology/*.ttl files cannot be distributed: tests that need them run ONLY on the owner's machine and skip themselves when the files are absent. No CI.

RECOMMENDED EXECUTION METHOD (the owner has not yet chosen; this is my recommendation): SUBAGENT-DRIVEN (superpowers:subagent-driven-development). Why: the tasks depend on each other's interfaces (EvaluationEngine/EvaluationOutcome, the result-graph contract, ReportBuilder.build(Model,Model,ReportContext)) and a mistake in the contract in Phase 1 would carry into every later task, so a fresh implementer plus a fresh reviewer per task catches it early. It costs a fresh context per task and per review, mostly in Phase 3 (rule engine), which is the longest. Alternative: NATIVE (superpowers:executing-plans), cheaper and faster but no independent review until the end. Ask the owner to confirm the method before starting.

STATE OF THE WORKING TREE (uncommitted, as of this note; last pushed commit 9368fd2)
Code: observation 'unit' in the API/store; unit-aware comparison (Quantities); evaluator accepts spec set forms (lists, set:intersection/union/difference, subclasses); held resources; TR290 ReportBuilder; JenaBuiltins (lexLess); chooseFrom rules (tio_choose.rules); lt/gt fixed to lessThan/greaterThan; seed rewritten in spec forms (log:allOf on the intent, explicit set:intersection, met:metric).
Tests: QuantitiesTest, JenaRulesTest, extended TurtleEvaluatorTest/HsiSeedIntentTest/ReportBuilderTest/TioReportIT.
Docs: README (observation unit), docs/Access_HSI_Demo.md, .gitignore (TR29*.pdf), docs/superpowers/{specs,plans}/.
Also modified: ontology/jena-rules/*.rules (functor fixes, tio_choose.rules). Do NOT commit .beads/interactions.jsonl.
Test status at the time: mvn test = 163 passed, 0 failed; integration = 26 of 27 pass (known failure bbf921j-dp2).

FIRST STEPS WHEN RESUMING
1. Confirm the execution method with the owner (recommendation above).
2. Task 0: run 'mvn test' (expect 163 passed) and 'mvn test -Dtest="*IT" -DfailIfNoTests=false' (expect only NegotiationIT.degradedToActive_flowTwo_afterFulfilledReEvaluation to fail), then commit the pending work in logical commits and push.
3. Continue with Task 1 of the plan; commit after each task.

THINGS TO KNOW
- Build tool is 'mvn' (there is no ./mvnw in the repo even though CLAUDE.md says so).
- Baseline gate for 'no behaviour change': unit suite fully green; integration green except bbf921j-dp2.
- The demos and all existing tests keep running on the java engine until the Jena engine is ready (Task 17).
- Scratch instances for manual checks must use other ports (e.g. -Dserver.port=8101 -Dintent.fuseki.port=3130 and a throwaway -Dintent.tdb2-path), because the owner's Docker container uses 8001/3030. Never touch the owner's container or its volume.
- 'docker compose down -v' needs --profile <name> (profile-gated services are skipped otherwise); the demo is started with APP_PROFILES=access,fuseki.
- CLAUDE.md still describes an InfModel/GenericRuleReasoner design that the code does not implement (README is accurate); Task 18 updates it. docs/12 - load_dlog.md explains where the old lt/gt bug in the supplied rules came from.
- Spec PDFs (docs/spec/TR29*.pdf) are gitignored (licensed); text copies can be regenerated with pdftotext -layout.
- Task 18 needs one owner decision: keep or retire HandlerStateWriter's handlerState graph (imo:conditionPassed).

RELATED OPEN ISSUES: bbf921j-dp2 (NegotiationIT Flow 2), bbf921j-3or (provider-aware S-tag), bbf921j-ed1 (VoIP filter demo coverage).
acceptance_criteria: Plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-18-evaluation-engines.md fully executed (Tasks 0-18); intent.evaluator selects java|jena|compare; conformance corpus passes on both engines; Jena engine ready; bbf921j-4qm closed

title: Evaluation should be driven by the Jena rule reasoner over the ontology model, not a hand-written Java evaluator
description:
INTENDED DESIGN (CLAUDE.md): for each evaluation TurtleEvaluator builds an ephemeral InfModel: load the intent expression + observations + resource data into a base Model together with the TIO ontology (the Turtle files in ontology/), wrap it in a GenericRuleReasoner loaded from the TIO rules (tio_all.rules), call prepare() so the rules materialise the inferred triples, then read the results (icm:result, imo:intentHandlingState, per-condition outcomes) with SPARQL on the inferred model. Custom Jena Builtins (set:setforAll, mf:mflogistic/mfpoly/mfmapping, quan:mean/median/sumOfSet) cover what rules cannot.

ACTUAL: the rules are never executed. JenaConfig loads src/main/resources/rules/tio_all.rules (122 rules) into a GenericRuleReasoner bean at startup, but nothing injects or calls it (no InfModel anywhere in src/main). TurtleEvaluator (~1100 lines of Java) makes every decision itself: it parses the Turtle, runs pre-processing passes, walks log:allOf lists, compares values with BigDecimal, evaluates set operators and delivery expectations by hand. The README describes this as 'a direct Java port of the Python 8-pass pipeline'. JenaBuiltins.java described in CLAUDE.md does not exist. The ontology TTL files are not loaded into the evaluation model (SchemaInit only loads them into the ontology named graph), and startup logs 'Rule references unimplemented functor: gt/lt' because the unused rule file references functors with no implementation.

WHY IT MATTERS: the Java evaluator re-implements, and can drift from, the semantics the ontology and rules define (e.g. TR290 delivery rule: a DeliveryExpectation is true iff a member of its target is an instance of deliveryType; reference rules in ontology/jena-rules and ontology/rules). New ontology/extension models (validity, guarantee, utility, preference, ProposalBestIntent) would need Java code instead of rules/data.

KNOWN GAPS TO RESOLVE IN THE CORRECTION: (1) the rules in tio_all.rules put icm:result on intent ELEMENTS, whereas TR290 s4 puts icm:result in REPORTS (IntentReport/ExpectationReport/ConditionReport via icm:about) - the rule set / report derivation needs aligning with the spec; (2) rules use functors gt/lt and others that are not implemented; the Builtins named in CLAUDE.md must be written; (3) chooseFrom/target selection, held resources (intent keeps its allocation), deterministic choice, nested pools filtered by a selected target and per-intent serialisation are implemented in Java today and need an equivalent in the rule-driven design (or an explicit hybrid boundary); (4) ontology/*.ttl is gitignored (proprietary) so the ontology is not in the repo - decide how it is supplied to build/test/Docker; (5) TR290 report tree (ElementResult/ReportTree/ReportBuilder) currently derives from the Java evaluator.

REGRESSION ORACLE: 139 unit tests (TurtleEvaluatorTest, HsiSeedIntentTest, ReportBuilderTest, HandlerStateWriterAllocationTest...) and the integration tests (AccessDemoIT, TioReportIT, ...) pin current behaviour; the rule-driven evaluator must pass them or the differences must be decided deliberately.

DECISIONS NEEDED: full rule-driven evaluation vs hybrid (rules for ontology reasoning/compliance, Java for selection/allocation); where the ontology files come from at build time; whether to keep or delete the unused reasoner bean and ontology/jena-rules, ontology/rules copies in the meantime. CLAUDE.md currently describes the intended design and should be left as the target until this is resolved (it is the README that is accurate about today).
acceptance_criteria: Evaluation of an intent runs through GenericRuleReasoner over a model that includes the ontology TTL files (InfModel.prepare + SPARQL for results); JenaBuiltins implemented for the referenced functors with no 'unimplemented functor' warnings; icm:result is produced per TR290 (in reports, not on intent elements); existing unit + integration tests pass or any behaviour change is agreed; CLAUDE.md and README describe the same design; ontology supply for build/test/Docker documented
notes: Design approved and implementation plan written 2026-10-18. Resume via bbf921j-5n4 (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-evaluation-engines-design.md and docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-18-evaluation-engines.md).

S-tag selection should be provider-aware (service provider owns the S-tag; C-tags only from that provider's S-tag)
description: Demo simplification today: the S-tag expectation picks the lowest-named pon:SVLANAllocation with serviceType HSIService, irrespective of who the service is for, and C-tags come from that S-VLAN. In reality the S-tag value identifies a service provider and a C-tag must only come from an S-tag belonging to that provider. Nothing models this: pon_resource_onto.ttl describes an S-tag per service type per OLT uplink assigned by the aggregation operator; no provider in the ontology, inventory data or intent. Also no look-ahead: if the chosen S-VLAN has no free C-tag the C-tag expectation fails although another HSI S-VLAN has some. Needs decisions: how the intent names the provider (context), where the provider<->S-tag<->OLT allocation lives, and the scope of an S-tag value (SVLAN-N-HSI and SVLAN-S-HSI both use S-tag 100 on different OLTs).

title: NegotiationIT.degradedToActive_flowTwo_afterFulfilledReEvaluation times out waiting for ACTIVE
description: Found when the integration tests first became runnable (httpclient5 test dependency added so TestRestTemplate can PATCH). The test PATCHes lifecycleStatus to DEGRADED, posts a passing observation (rtt=30 < 100) and expects Flow 2 (DEGRADED -> ACTIVE on Fulfilled) within 10s; it never reaches ACTIVE. Reproduces on a clean checkout of the last pushed commit (before the delivery-expectation changes), so it is not caused by them. The other 24 integration tests pass. Investigate whether Flow 2 in EvaluationDispatcher is broken or the test setup (FSM transition / timing) is wrong.
acceptance_criteria: NegotiationIT passes (all 6 tests); root cause recorded

Access demo data does not exercise the HSI service-type filter for S-VLAN/C-tag selection
description: The seed intent limits S-tag and C-tag selection to S-VLANs whose pon:serviceType is pon:HSIService. In BBF_access/pon_resource_data.ttl SVLAN-N-VoIP (serviceType VoIPService) has no C-tags and is never a candidate anyway, so removing the filter would not change any demo result. The filter is only proven by unit tests (TurtleEvaluatorTest pool_filteredByPropertyOfAnotherPool, HsiSeedIntentTest.noHsiSVlans_stagAndCtagCannotBeDelivered). Add VoIP C-tags (free, lowest names so they would be picked first if unfiltered) to the demo inventory and an Access_HSI_Demo step or check showing they are never selected for HSI.
acceptance_criteria: Demo inventory has free C-tags on SVLAN-N-VoIP that sort before the HSI ones; Access_HSI_Demo shows an HSI intent never selects them; unit test covers it
